title: Machine learning selects cell-death genes in COPD tested with an herbal formula in rats
summary: Mendelian randomization screened 439 programmed-cell-death genes with genetic causal links to COPD; intersection with transcriptomic and co-expression analyses and several machine-learning algorithms selected five diagnostic markers (NT5E, SPP1, BLK, PLAT, LGMN). Single-cell analysis and virtual perturbation suggested a bidirectional role for LGMN. In a rat COPD model, the traditional Chinese medicine formula Feizhangning dose-dependently lowered IL-1beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha in serum and lavage fluid and reversed the abnormal mRNA and protein expression of the five genes. This is a non-peer-reviewed preprint; docking and network pharmacology are computational, diagnostic performance and animal numbers were not reviewed, and no human test is reported.
ai_technology: Multiple machine-learning feature-selection algorithms (14 listed in the linked data deposit, with SHAP) select diagnostic genes from COPD transcriptomes.
organization: Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

evidence.tested: Expression of the five ML-selected genes and inflammatory cytokines measured in a rat COPD model treated with Feizhangning.
evidence.unknown: Which algorithm selected the final genes and its diagnostic metrics, rat group sizes, causal role of the genes, human efficacy; full text not reviewed. A data and code deposit (ScienceDB, 2026-11-03) preceded the preprint but states no results.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning algorithms selected the five diagnostic genes whose expression was then measured under treatment in rats.

source_review.scope: Independent review: abstract from Europe PMC, Crossref posting date, OpenAlex title search; linked ScienceDB data deposit description read. Full text not read.
